definition: Buzz is an open-source multi-user harness for large language model agents and a workplace collaboration application developed by Block, Inc.
details: It was announced by Block co-founder Jack Dorsey on July 21, 2026. Buzz allows multiple human users and AI agents to participate in shared channels, with each user or agent assigned a separate cryptographic identity. It combines group messaging with agent orchestration, software repositories and automated workflows. The software uses a self-hostable Nostr relay, on which messages, reactions, workflow actions and Git events are recorded as signed events. Its agent harness supports external coding agents through the Agent Client Protocol. As of late July, the repository grew to 2,000+ commits, 100+ contributors, 22,000+ followers (stars), and 2,500+ forks.

explainer.lead: Buzz is Block’s open-source workspace where people and AI agents can collaborate in shared channels, coordinate coding work, and run automated workflows. Announced by Block co-founder Jack Dorsey on July 21, 2026, it keeps a signed record of activity on a relay that teams can host themselves.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a clubhouse where classmates and robot helpers work on projects together. Everyone gets their own secure name tag, and the clubhouse notebook records messages, reactions, and changes to the project. Buzz works like that, helping a whole team keep track of what people and AI helpers are doing.
tiers.practitioner: Teams can self-host Buzz’s Nostr relay and connect external coding agents through the Agent Client Protocol. Shared channels combine discussion, agent orchestration, software repositories, and workflows, while signed events record messages, reactions, workflow actions, and Git activity. Buzz coordinates models and agents rather than providing a language model itself.
tiers.paperLevel: Buzz can be described as a multi-user agent harness over a signed-event collaboration log: each human or agent has a distinct cryptographic identity, and messages, reactions, workflow actions, and Git events are recorded on a self-hostable Nostr relay. External coding agents interface with the harness through the Agent Client Protocol.

explainer.example: A developer posts a bug in a shared channel, and an external coding agent connected through the Agent Client Protocol works on a fix. The discussion, workflow actions, and resulting Git events are signed and recorded on the relay, so teammates can follow the work in the same workspace.

usedIn.name: Agent-assisted software development
usedIn.detail: External coding agents can work alongside developers through shared channels and connected repositories.

usedIn.name: Workplace collaboration
usedIn.detail: Teams can combine group messaging with automated workflows and agent coordination.

usedIn.name: Self-hosted team infrastructure
usedIn.detail: Organizations can run the Nostr relay that stores the workspace’s signed events.

explainer.intuition: Buzz is less like a single chatbot and more like a shared workroom: people and agents enter with separate identities, communicate in channels, and leave a signed trail of their collaboration.
howItWorks: A self-hostable Nostr relay records messages, reactions, workflow actions, and Git events as signed events. The agent harness orchestrates AI participants and supports external coding agents through the Agent Client Protocol, alongside repositories and automated workflows.
explainer.whyItMatters: Buzz brings human discussion, agent activity, code changes, and automation into one collaboration environment. Separate cryptographic identities and signed events make it possible to distinguish participants and track their actions.
misconceptions: Buzz is not a large language model; it is a collaboration application and agent harness.
It is not only a group-chat application; it also includes repositories and automated workflows.
Its coding agents can be external tools connected through the Agent Client Protocol.
Its Nostr relay can be self-hosted.
